source: Re-traced by hand on the router body (ctx/skill), the way the audit traced the old body (census-skill 10-routing-test.mjs): for each request, the SKILL.md line that gives the route (anchor: that line, verbatim), the references the route tells the agent to read (whole files are what a client loads), and the reader verdict. top_down_* is what a top-down reader loads before the first correct command: body lines 1 to the route line, plus the reference from its top to the first command (o200k); top_down_tokens_cli adds the CLI paragraph where the command needs it. This is a reading, not a run of agents. Redo the trace whenever the body changes: see README.md. Re-traced on 2026-11-21 for the routing follow-up: line numbers moved by the new first-step lines; R8, R13 and R14 anchors changed wording, and every route stays clear.

previous_trace.note: router body before the routing follow-up (decisions 1, 2, 5 and 6)

requests.request: Here is /opt/acme/bin/licensed, a Linux ELF. Explain how it validates the licence key.
requests.anchor: - Explain or decompile a native program or library → `open_binary`, `search_procedures` or `search_strings`, then `analyze_function`
requests.first_command: open_binary, search_strings or search_procedures, then analyze_function (CLI: rea search / rea function <path> <name>, body lines 45-53)
requests.note: First-step line for a native program. No provider is installed in this environment, so the call itself ends at provider_unavailable; the refusal rule (body 'When a step is refused') names the inspectors that still work. A CLI agent also reads the CLI paragraph (body lines 45-53) for rea search / rea function. Re-traced after the routing follow-up: the refusal rule now names rea inspect-with-objdump and rea debug-with-gdb, and the provider refusal lists both with the file's path.

requests.request: Find where app-release.apk builds its login request.
requests.note: One line. The JADX requirement is in the tool's refusal, which names the download (seen here).

requests.request: How does this Electron app (app.asar) implement auto-update?
requests.anchor: - Electron app, ASAR or JavaScript tree → `analyze_javascript_application` with `detail: "summary"`
requests.note: The line itself asks for the summary, and rule 1 above it gives the CLI form. Seen here: the summary of a three-file app is about 3,000 tokens against 112,519 by default.

requests.request: Rebuild the web app at http://127.0.0.1:4000 as new code under a new name and tell me when it matches. I can reset it.
requests.anchor: - Rebuild or clone a web app the user can run and reset → read [clone-runs](references/clone-runs.md) before touching the original; then `rea init-clone-run`
requests.first_command: rea init-clone-run <dir> with the answers the lead card asks for (clone-runs.md lines 126-140)
requests.note: First line of the list. The client then loads the whole playbook (clone-runs.md); the lead card's ask-once list ends at its line 140. The command's flags are in rea init-clone-run --help.

requests.request: The service crashed; here is core.1234 and the binary. What happened?
requests.anchor: - A crash (Linux core or Apple `.ips` file) → `inspect_recorded_crash` (amd64 or AArch64 core; needs pwntools), `inspect_apple_ips`
requests.note: States amd64 or AArch64 and pwntools. Seen here: the tool refuses without REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON and names it.

requests.request: Here is router firmware fw-2.1.bin. What is inside, and is there a hard-coded password?
requests.anchor: - Inside an archive, installer, app bundle or firmware image → `open_binary`, then `inspect_artifact`; firmware it cannot map: `inspect_firmware_regions` (needs Binwalk)
requests.first_command: open_binary then inspect_artifact; inspect_firmware_regions (Binwalk) when it cannot map the image
requests.note: Two steps in order: inspect_artifact maps container formats (seen here on a built uImage); for an image it cannot map, inspect_firmware_regions, which needs Binwalk (its refusal names REA_BINWALK_COMMAND).

requests.request: Here are v3.1 and v3.2 of the vendor's Linux agent binary. What changed in the update check?
requests.anchor: - Two versions → native: `list_procedures` of each, `match_native_functions`; JavaScript: analyze each, `compare_application_versions`; packages: `inspect_artifact` each, `compare_artifacts`
requests.first_command: open_binary and list_procedures on each build, then match_native_functions (MCP only)
requests.note: One line for native, JavaScript and packages. The native leg needs a provider and was not run here; the JavaScript leg (compare_application_versions on two analyzed trees) and the package leg (compare_artifacts on two inspected zips) ran.

requests.request: This is main.4f2a.js, minified, from the site. Recover readable source and tell me how it signs requests.
requests.anchor: - One JavaScript file → analyze its directory, or `recover_javascript_sources` (needs Wakaru)
requests.first_command: recover_javascript_sources {path, output_directory} (needs Wakaru), or the file alone in a directory, then analyze_javascript_application
requests.note: Was wrong (analyze_javascript_application refuses a single file). Seen here: recover_javascript_sources refuses without Wakaru and names it; analyze_javascript_application on a directory holding only the file works. Re-traced after the routing follow-up: the line now says to analyze the file's directory (analyze_javascript_application) or recover it with Wakaru; inspect_artifact on the file also names analyze-javascript-application on its directory as its first probe. Clear.

requests.request: Which API endpoints does the checkout page call? I have it open in Chrome.
requests.anchor: - What a page open in the user's browser calls → `list_browser_targets`, then `inspect_web_page` with `allowed_origins` listing the page and API origins
requests.first_command: list_browser_targets {cdp_endpoint}, then inspect_web_page with allowed_origins naming the page and API origins
requests.note: Was ambiguous (three bullets, one naming no tool, and observe_web_session records navigation only). Seen here on a local page that calls another origin: inspect_web_page with allowed_origins lists that request; with the default scope it is excluded and completeness.excluded counts it.

requests.request: What does Acme.Licensing.dll (.NET) do with the registry?
I recorded checkout.har on staging. Build an agent environment from it.
requests.anchor: - An agent environment → from a HAR: `rea environment-build <file.har> <new dir>`; a live web app: [environments](references/environments.md); a Linux desktop app with a task: [desktop-build](references/desktop-build.md)
requests.note: Was ambiguous (two bullets; the command only in the guide). The line gives the command. Seen here: a HAR built into an environment.

requests.request: Build me a GIMP environment where the agent crops a photo to a square.
requests.anchor: - An agent environment → from a HAR: `rea environment-build <file.har> <new dir>`; a live web app: [environments](references/environments.md); a Linux desktop app with a task: [desktop-build](references/desktop-build.md)
requests.note: The line sends the agent to desktop-build.md, which a client loads whole; its first command is at its line 337, after the install and app-driving notes the build needs.

requests.request: What does the app keep in app.db?
requests.anchor: - One fact about a file (hardening, imports, dependencies, signing, a database) → its inspector by path, no provider: `inspect_binary_hardening`, `inspect_elf_dependencies`, `inspect_sqlite_database`
requests.note: Was late (53rd bullet). One line. Seen here: the tool refuses on Node 22 and names Node 24.15.

requests.request: Is /usr/sbin/sshd built with PIE, RELRO and stack canaries?
requests.anchor: - One fact about a file (hardening, imports, dependencies, signing, a database) → its inspector by path, no provider: `inspect_binary_hardening`, `inspect_elf_dependencies`, `inspect_sqlite_database`
requests.note: Was late and overlapping. One line, the portable inspector.

requests.request: Run ./migrate --dry-run and tell me which files it touches and what it prints.
requests.anchor: - What a program does when run → `capture_process_scenario`, `dry_run: true` first
requests.first_command: capture_process_scenario {executable, arguments, filesystem_observation_paths, dry_run: true} (CLI: rea capture-process <file>, body lines 49-51)
requests.note: Was blocked on the CLI. Body lines 49-51 give the scenario file's fields. Seen here: rea capture-process with those fields, dry run and real run (the created file was reported).
